RNA transcript detection versus cell-surface protein abundance: CELLxGENE Census stores single-cell/single-nucleus RNA UMI counts (X['raw']) and does not expose paired CITE-seq ADT surface-protein abundance or post-translational surface density, which govern functional receptor engagement (such as CD28 superagonist binding in CD4+ effector-memory T cells).

Cell-type annotation and suspension-type non-equivalence: generic 'T cell' (CL:0000084) annotations in non-lymphoid parenchyma or single-nucleus RNA-seq (fc6ef080-9e5f-4aea-b9c4-a45a208bd288) pool CD4+, CD8+, gamma-delta, and regulatory T cells and sample only nuclear pre-mRNA/mRNA, making them biologically and technically incomparable to whole-cell peripheral blood CD4+ effector-memory T cells.

Cross-dataset normalisation and batch effects: CELLxGENE Census release 2025-11-08 provides raw UMI counts (X['raw']) without a cross-species batch-corrected expression layer; direct numerical comparison across independent studies, chemistries, and reference genome builds (GRCh38 vs Mmul_10) is confounded without matched experimental design.

findings.claim: Rhesus macaque CD4+ effector memory T cells are CD28-negative, whereas human CD4+ effector memory T cells are CD28-positive.
findings.mechanism: CD4+ effector memory T cells are the predominant source of cytokines released by TGN1412 in humans; because rhesus macaque CD4+ effector memory T cells lack CD28, the animal model does not activate these cells upon CD28 stimulation and fails to replicate cytokine release.
findings.scepticNote: The cited literature directly supports the loss of CD28 expression on rhesus macaque CD4+ effector memory T cells compared to human, but this reflects curated experimental literature rather than primary single-cell dataset concordance.
